title: Ukraine's biggest drone raid hits the Crimean Bridge, three US carriers gather, and the Houthis reach the strait
summary: Russia says it shot down a record thirteen hundred Ukrainian drones in a raid that struck the Crimean Bridge and oil sites, the carrier Theodore Roosevelt is reported in the Middle East alongside two others, the Houthis move into the coast above the Bab el-Mandeb strait and close on Aden, Israel strikes a weapons shipment in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, and Iran rules out nuclear inspections until the war ends.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Monday, November sixteenth. And overnight, Ukraine launched what looks like its largest drone attack on Russia of the entire war.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted one thousand three hundred and thirty-six Ukrainian drones in a single night. That's the most it has ever claimed. Moscow's mayor says about six hundred of them were heading for the Moscow region. He says a hundred and ninety-one were shot down as they neared the city.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And one target stands out. The Crimean Bridge.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. Crimea's Russian-installed governor says the bridge was struck, and traffic was restricted. The Kremlin's spokesman called the damage insignificant. We don't have independent confirmation of how bad it is.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The oil campaign continued too. Ukraine's General Staff says its drones hit processing units at the Ilsky refinery, in Russia's Krasnodar region. Local officials reported a fire at an industrial site, and six people injured by falling debris, including children.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Azov, in the Rostov region, the governor says drone attacks started fires at four industrial facilities and injured three people. A Ukrainian monitoring channel says an oil depot was burning there.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And a day earlier, deep inside Russia, Ukraine says it hit a petrochemical plant and a refinery in Nizhnekamsk, in Tatarstan. Local authorities confirmed industrial damage, and three people were injured.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: President Zelensky now says more than fifty-five percent of Russia's refining capacity has been knocked out. Bloomberg's estimate is lower, about forty percent offline. Either way, it's a very large share.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And it's being felt inside Russia. The Institute for the Study of War says the strikes on oil infrastructure have had knock-on effects on fuel supply, and that Russian authorities have brought back some limits on fuel sales.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: All of this is happening while the diplomacy is on hold. Last week's talks produced an agreement in principle to exchange up to thirteen hundred prisoners each, and a promise that Europe will join the next round. But there's still no date for either.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Russia struck Ukraine as well, though on a smaller scale. Ukraine's Air Force counted a hundred and fifty-eight attack drones overnight. One person was killed and three injured in Dnipro. One was killed and four wounded in the Kharkiv region.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Institute for the Study of War makes a point about why Russia's strikes on the power grid are getting through. It says Russian forces are exploiting speed restrictions on drones that use the Starshield satellite network, which Ukraine relies on for interception.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ground, the Institute reports a Russian infiltration mission north of Kupiansk, but no confirmed advances. One more item from its report. Estonia says it will close its border with Russia after an attempted arson attack.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now to the Middle East, and the ships. American officials have told The National and Stars and Stripes that the carrier Theodore Roosevelt entered Central Command's area on Sunday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That makes three American carriers in the region. The Roosevelt, the George Washington, and the George H. W. Bush. Central Command hasn't officially confirmed the arrival.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Roosevelt carries Carrier Air Wing Eleven, and it's escorted by the cruiser Chosin and the destroyers Paul Hamilton and Decatur.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So that's a lot of firepower arriving at a tense moment.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And it's not clear how long all three will stay. The Roosevelt was expected to relieve the George Washington, which has been there since August. For now, reports say the George Washington is staying put.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That arrival comes right after two Iranian drone attacks aimed at American radar sites in Bahrain, on Friday and Sunday. Both were reported intercepted. Bahrain says it holds Iran fully responsible.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iran, for its part, is digging in. It says there will be no United Nations inspections of its damaged nuclear sites until the war is, quote, permanently ended. And its foreign minister says a group of ten regional countries has backed Tehran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under an initial ceasefire.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's go to Yemen, because yesterday's story has moved quickly. Yesterday, Saudi-backed forces pulled back from the coast near the Bab el-Mandeb strait. Today, the Houthis are there.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Houthi military sources told the news agency AFP that their fighters have deployed along more than a hundred and fifty kilometres of coastline, from Dhubab to a place called Khor Omairah.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And military and government sources say the Houthis are now within about sixty kilometres of Aden, the government's temporary capital. A government spokesperson admitted the withdrawal left a vacuum that the Houthis filled.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So we've added that stretch of coast to the armed-groups layer on the map, marked as contested, because control there is very recent and still fluid. It matters for shipping. Bab el-Mandeb is the southern gate of the Red Sea, and the Strait of Hormuz is already disrupted.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Lebanon, something unusual. The Israeli military says it struck a weapons shipment bound for Hezbollah at Janta, in the Beqaa Valley near the Syrian border, at about four thirty this morning.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Lebanese media say it's the first Israeli strike in the Beqaa in three months. No casualties were officially reported. Israel also says it demolished a thirty-five metre tunnel in the southern town of Majdal Zoun.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And a reminder from the weekend in Gaza. Israel and Hamas both confirmed that the commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade, Samir Abu Younis, was killed in a strike in al-Mawasi on Saturday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Saudi Arabia on Sunday, the coalition said it shot down two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, plus drones over the Eastern Province. No damage was reported.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: One housekeeping note. Yesterday's update to the site didn't go live on time, so today's update carries both days. The strike archive now holds a hundred and forty-two entries.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Russia's response to the bridge attack and the record drone raid. Whether three carriers near Iran is a rotation or a build-up. And how far the Houthis push toward Aden.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
